name: Huchiun-Aguasto Ohlone village at Tormey (Rodeo) - the 400-500 of 1776
shape_note: Domed/conical tule-thatched family house on a bent-willow pole frame, about 3-5 m across (as in early_sf.csv; Milliken 2009 ch.3). Count is an ESTIMATE at ~6-8 people per house. Anza's party camped at Rodeo Creek on 1 Apr 1776 and next morning passed through a village of 'some four hundred persons' (Font) / 'about five hundred souls' (Anza) 'in a little valley on the bank of a small arroyo', less than a quarter league east of camp; Bolton identifies it 'at Tormey'. The largest Bay Area village reported by the Spaniards (also Canizares 1775); Milliken suspects a seasonal gathering place. Local tribe Huchiun-Aguasto (San Francisco Bay Costanoan); they moved to Mission Dolores 1803-1810, the last with the Carquins in Jun 1809 - Feb 1810 (Milliken 2009 ch.5). SUPERSEDES early_region hch_aguasto_village (same village, placed by guess near Pinole Creek with end 1800). Position precision ~1 km (Bolton's identification of Font's/Anza's village). name: Ewu, Coast Miwok village on Gallinas Creek (San Rafael)
shape_note: Coast Miwok kotcha: conical house of tule slabs or redwood bark over a pole frame, ~3-5 m across (Wikipedia 'Coast Miwok', after Barrett 1908 / Kelly). Count is an ESTIMATE at ~6-8 people per house. Kelly (1978:415, after Barrett 1908) put Ewu at Gallinas Creek, one of four located San Rafael-vicinity villages; Mission San Rafael converts from 'Echaguali', 'Eguali', 'Heuali' may refer to it. Tamal Aguasto / Miller Creek Tamal community (~395 people); half baptized by Jan 1803, the last significant Miller Creek group in 1808 (Milliken 2009 Coast Miwok ch.9). Position ESTIMATED on the lower creek. Position precision ~1.5 km (creek named by Kelly / Barrett). Placed at the published place-level precision only (no archaeological site record used).

name: Etcakolum (Echacolom), Coast Miwok village on Tomales Bay south of Marshall
shape_note: Coast Miwok kotcha: conical house of tule slabs or redwood bark over a pole frame, ~3-5 m across (Wikipedia 'Coast Miwok', after Barrett 1908 / Kelly). Count is an ESTIMATE at ~6-8 people per house. 'Etcakolum, two miles south of Marshall, is the only specific village location documented for the South Tomales Bay region by early twentieth century ethnographers (Barrett 1908a:308; Collier and Thalman 1991:6). It is certainly equivalent to Echacolom of the Mission San Rafael records' (Milliken 2009 Coast Miwok ch.10). South Tomales Bay people (~780, CDM) were baptized at Mission Dolores 1813-17 and San Rafael from 1818. End ESTIMATED. Position precision ~1 km (2 miles south of Marshall). Placed at the published place-level precision only (no archaeological site record used). Point moved 672 m onto dry ground of the terrain's c.1800 land cover.
